hints: Focus on the structures first, propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol while propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, so think about how their oxidation differs.
Remember that mild oxidation turns the primary alcohol into an aldehyde (propanal) but turns the secondary alcohol into a ketone (propanone).
Now ask yourself which familiar test gives a positive result with aldehydes but stays negative with ketones to complete the distinction.
walkthrough:
**Identify the alcohol types**

Think side by side with the structures. Propan-1-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, with the OH on the end carbon, so it is primary. Propan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, with the OH in the middle, so it is secondary.

This difference controls what they form on oxidation.

**Predict the mild oxidation products**

A primary alcohol oxidises in two stages, first to an aldehyde, then to a carboxylic acid. A secondary alcohol oxidises in one stage to a ketone and stops there.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$$

**Use Fehling's to tell aldehyde from ketone**

Fehling's reagent is a specific test for aldehydes. On warming, an aldehyde reduces the blue $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ complex to a brick-red precipitate of $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$.

$$\text{RCHO + 2Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Ketones are not oxidised by Fehling's, so no colour change occurs. That gives a clear yes or no distinction.

options.A: Both alcohols are oxidised by hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$. The purple solution is decolourised in both cases, so you see the same observation and cannot distinguish them.
options.B: Both alcohols are oxidised by hot acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$. The orange solution turns green in both cases, so again there is no difference to observe.
options.C: Both alcohols dehydrate with concentrated acid to give the same alkene, propene ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$). Propene then decolourises $\text{Br}_2(aq)$ in both cases, so this is not distinguishing.
options.D: Mild oxidation gives different carbonyls: propanal (an aldehyde) from propan-1-ol and propanone (a ketone) from propan-2-ol. Only propanal gives a positive Fehling's test with a brick-red precipitate on warming, while propanone gives no change, so this clearly distinguishes them.
